current_episode.title: The Otago Opportunity - Episode 16 - Good Good

guest.bio_context: Rose Gleeson trained as a chef for two years at Otago Polytechnic and worked two years in the restaurant industry before moving into government roles at ACC and Dunedin City Council. She represented New Zealand in synchronized figure skating at the 2009 World Championships in Zagreb, Croatia. She has also written a published children's book and performed in an improv troupe. At the time of the interview, she holds a full-time day job alongside owning Good Good, which she purchased approximately one year prior.

key_stats: Good Good has a maximum venue capacity of 40 people, due to fire exit regulations requiring access through neighboring business Big Lizard
Minimum wage when Rose Gleeson worked as a chef was NZ$13 per hour, with weeks sometimes reaching 70 hours
Rose trained at Otago Polytechnic for 2 years to become a chef, then worked 2 years in the restaurant industry
New Zealand's synchronized figure skating team placed 21st out of 21 teams at the 2009 World Championships in Zagreb
Events at Good Good with a 40-person cap would require per-head spending of NZ$60–$70 to be financially viable
Duty manager LCQ qualification and manager's certificate each cost a couple of hundred dollars, and candidates must be aged 20+ with 6 months of supervised experience in a licensed premises
context.transcript_excerpt: Coming up on the Otago Opportunity, we're talking to Rose Gleeson, the owner of Good Good in Vogel Street, Dunedin. This is the Otago Opportunity, a limited series look at the future of our province. I'm your host, Pauline Moore, and in this series, we're taking the policies of the Opportunity Party and moving them out of the Wellington think tank and into our own backyard here in Dunedin. Each week we'll hear from local business owners, students and families about how a tax reset or a citizen's assembly would actually impact their daily lives. It's not about the politics, it's about the future of the place we call home. Welcome to the Otago Opportunity. Kia ora and welcome to the Otago Opportunity. Joining me today is Dave Bainbridge-Safar, the Opportunity candidate for Dunedin and our guest, Rose Gleeson, the owner of Good Good in Vogel Street, Dunedin, arguably the top burger joint in town. Welcome. Kia ora. Now, Good Good is in Vogel Street in Dunedin, as I said, which is a pretty cool part of town. Can you explain, Rose, what the vibe of the restaurant is for those that haven't been there? I've kind of started likening it to Grandma Grunge because it's sort of an array of old granny couches that are kind of around the side of it. But then there's quite a cool graffiti vibe as well. So it sort of mixes like a grungy industrial with very comfortable, familiar, old couches. Excellent. That's giving us a good picture. And how long have you owned this business? How did you get into it? So we are coming up to a year now, so I think it'll be a year in August. I had, to be honest, it's always been my dream to run a burger place. Burgers have just been my absolute favorite food forever. And I had always thought Good Good was just the coolest place in the whole entire world. It was my favorite place in Dunedin to go to, and I kind of saw it was up for sale and I thought, oh no, someone's going to ruin it, someone's going to come along, and I thought, well, may as well give it a try myself. But thankfully, we're still going pretty strong. Yeah, it's been a bumpy, you can kind of see where the economy started to recover late last year, and then where the economy absolutely tanked again in February. So it's been a journey, that's for sure. Just to be clear, we're not having cause and effect there. We're not suggesting that, Rose, your acquisition of Good Good was what led to the economy tanking. We're not saying that. I have no idea, to be honest. Nothing's possible in this day and age, Dave. Maybe it was me. And full disclosure, Rose and I worked together at Dunedin City Council. And I do recall, Rose, you and a couple of colleagues, I think, did go on a burger tour once a week of all the different restaurants. And you were testing out which was the best burger in Dunedin. Was the answer Good Good, or did you find a better burger? I mean, at the time, I was always going to say Good Good. I think it's stood the test of time. It's pretty strong. Yeah, I just I'm just trying to remember. You've got a really good memory, Dave. I mean, I genuinely do think Good Good is, before you bought it, I thought it was the best burger place in Dunedin. And certainly after you've owned it, I've been there a few times and it is still, I think, the best burger place in Dunedin. Yeah. It's been a crazy year owning it, though. What are the biggest kind of challenges you've had since you bought the place? Well, the changeover didn't go super smoothly. I accidentally signed up for somebody else's power. So Good Good power got cut off and we had to scramble to try and figure out why, because I was saying, no, I've signed up for power. I've got my account here, I've been billed. No, I mean, I had to contact whose power I did sign up for and tell them they had to re-sign up for the power. pending_qa.q: What were Rose Gleeson's synchronized figure skating achievements?
pending_qa.r: Rose Gleeson was part of New Zealand's first-ever representative synchronized figure skating team sent to the World Championships in 2009, held in Zagreb, Croatia. The team finished 21st out of 21 competing teams. The trip involved a one-week training camp in Auckland, a stopover training session in Los Angeles, and travel through Germany before reaching Zagreb.
